payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image visibly present its content as a drawing rather than as a photograph with blur or texture overlays?
node.criteria: pass: substantial depicted content has clearly drawn or illustrated rendering, not merely softened contours or texture over photographic detail; fail: the content remains clearly photographic without a genuine drawing conversion; unknown: evidence does not reliably distinguish a drawing from filtered photographic detail.
node.binding: Assess only drawing-versus-photographic rendering. Do not assess chalk medium; do not treat blur, grain, or softened contours alone as proof of a drawing.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image renders the giraffes and surroundings with visibly illustrated, sketch-like contours and simplified shading rather than retaining the source photograph’s detailed photographic appearance. This supports a drawing conversion; chalk medium is not assessed here.
The edited image retains photographic detail and recognizable photo-like giraffes and scenery, with blur and grainy texture overlays rather than a clearly drawn or illustrated rendering.

The edited image renders the giraffes and surroundings with visibly illustrated, sketch-like contours and simplified, painterly forms rather than retaining clear photographic detail. This supports a drawing conversion; the chalk medium is not assessed here.

The edited image retains photographic detail and recognizable photo-like giraffe and landscape rendering, with blur and grain-like texture overlays rather than a clearly drawn or illustrated conversion.

The edited image renders the giraffes and surroundings with visibly illustrated, hand-drawn contours and shading rather than retaining photographic detail with only blur or texture. This assesses drawing conversion only, not whether the medium is chalk.

n3: The node’s main weakness is inconsistent aggregation: identical support patterns (n1 pass for chalk-like treatment, n2 fail because photographic detail remains) yield partial in two traces, while both-pass traces yield complete. Preserve that distinction, but make the complete criterion require affirmative support for both chalk medium and drawing conversion across the image; do not let n1’s chalk-like texture plus n2’s merely sketch-like cues automatically establish a full conversion. Conversely, treat retained photographic detail as evidence against complete conversion, not proof that no requested change occurred: n1’s dusty texture and smudged/sketchy marks are affirmative partial progress. Keep absent reserved for both supports affirmatively showing no progress, and unknown for insufficient evidence. The edited image visibly has a chalky, smudged treatment and softened outlines, while the giraffes and scene remain recognizable and substantially photo-derived, so partial is supported; the traces are valid and queried, with no transport or dependency failures. Clarify the evidence threshold for distinguishing a genuine drawing conversion from a texture/blur overlay, and apply it consistently rather than allowing wording variation or confidence to flip the outcome.
